title: Choose the dashboard layout
question: The look is already set by DESIGN.md; this round picks how the dashboard is organised. The roll dealt three structures. Lock one, steer, or re-roll.

options.label: Request path
options.thesis: Your stack drawn as the path a request takes: Browser, Apache, PHP, MySQL, with the broken link shown where it breaks.
materials: station tiles on a hairline path
options.viewport: Left rail with Dashboard, Sites, Versions, Database; a horizontal path of four stations with live state and Start/Stop; the selected station's log underneath.
options.risk: Fewer rows fit at once than a table; with many services (Redis, mail) the path needs a second row.

options.label: Command-first
options.thesis: A command bar does everything (start, stop, open logs); the service list below is a dense readout.
options.viewport: Command bar across the top with Ctrl+K; dense service rows with inline actions; recent activity on the right.
options.risk: Fast for professionals, but students may not discover the command bar.

options.label: Top tabs and cards
options.thesis: Tabs across the top for each area; one card per service with its facts and buttons.
options.viewport: Brand and tabs (Services, Sites, Versions, Database) in a top bar; a 2x2 grid of service cards; logs open per card.
options.risk: Same-size cards are the generic dashboard default and spread data apart, so comparing ports and states takes longer.
